nodes.label: OSC Internal Knowledge Assistant
nodes.rationale: A provider-agnostic RAG question-answering service over OSC's internal documents. Phase 5: measured, observable, durably logged, operable; not production-ready because there is no authentication, no per-document ACLs, no rate limiting and no conversation persistence.

nodes.label: Vendor Agnosticism
nodes.rationale: Chat model, embedding model, reranker, vector store and chunker are each selected by configuration and swappable independently. Business logic imports only `protocols` and `types` and never a provider module — a rule that is grep-checkable, which is what makes the agnosticism real rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: The Five Protocol Seams
nodes.rationale: ChatModel, EmbeddingModel, VectorStore, Reranker and Chunker are Protocols satisfied structurally — no base class, no inheritance — so a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, which is what makes the API and CLI tests meaningful.

nodes.label: StoreInspector — Optional Inspection Protocol
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not part of VectorStore: every VectorStore method is one a new store must implement to be usable at all, whereas a hosted vector DB exposing no aggregate API should still be a perfectly good VectorStore. Tooling probes with isinstance and reports absence rather than failing.

nodes.label: Container — Composition Root and Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Builds components lazily via cached_property so `ingest` never constructs a chat model and never needs an LLM credential. Shutdown releases exactly what was built, because cached_property's presence in the instance __dict__ is the record of construction; components are probed for aclose()/close() rather than required to have one.

nodes.label: Registry Wiring — Providers as Additions
nodes.rationale: Five Registry instances map provider name to factory; a provider module registers itself on import. Adding a provider is a new file plus one import line, so nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation.

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.rationale: Internal corpora are dense with acronyms, codenames and error strings that semantic search handles badly, and paraphrase that keyword search handles badly. RRF is implemented identically in fusion.py and in pgvector SQL so both stores rank identically. Avoiding a known failure mode, not premature optimisation.
nodes.norm_label: hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion

nodes.label: Architectural Abstention Policy
nodes.rationale: No retrieval hits means the model is never called; no citations means the answer is treated as ungrounded. A guarantee in the code path rather than a prompt instruction. In streaming mode the final `complete` event is authoritative.

nodes.label: Citation Strength Differs by Provider, Silently
nodes.rationale: Anthropic returns citations verified against source text; every other provider asserts them via [n] markers a model can emit for an unsupported claim. Both produce the same Citation shape so nothing downstream can tell the difference — a deliberate trade-off for vendor agnosticism.
nodes.norm_label: citation strength differs by provider, silently

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts
nodes.rationale: System prompts are module constants with no interpolation. Anything dynamic would break prefix caching for every request and make evaluation results unattributable to a configuration.

nodes.label: Observability Layer — trace, store, render
nodes.rationale: Three modules with one dependency direction — trace collects, store persists, render presents — composed only in the package __init__. span() outside a trace returns a detached span recording nothing, so instrumented code carries no `if tracing` branches; a nested trace() extends rather than forks, which lets retrieve be both a whole operation and a stage.

nodes.label: Instrument the Pipeline, Not the Adapter
nodes.rationale: Every provider call is made from a pipeline, so wrapping the call sites covers all 37 providers without a single adapter importing the tracer — and a new provider is traced the day it is written.
nodes.norm_label: instrument the pipeline, not the adapter

nodes.label: Bounded Append-Only JSONL Trace Store
nodes.rationale: An in-memory ring buffer works for a long-lived server but not for a CLI process that exits when the answer prints. Chosen over re-running with --explain (a generation is not deterministic, so you get *a* trace not *the* trace), a Postgres traces table (write load on the primary datastore, unavailable when the DB is what broke), OpenTelemetry plus a collector (right once traces leave the host, wrong for reading one in a terminal) and a daemon. Rotation not rewriting, so appending is O(1); writing never raises.

nodes.label: Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Built in-repo rather than adopting RAGAS/TruLens/DeepEval: each is LLM-judge-first so the CI-gating metrics would be the non-deterministic ones, each imposes its own data model on the code path most in need of reading, and the metrics themselves are twenty lines of set arithmetic. It drives the real pipelines built by the real Container, because an evaluation against a special code path measures the special code path.

nodes.label: Deterministic Metrics Gate CI; the LLM Judge Is Opt-In
nodes.rationale: A gate that can change its mind between two runs of the same commit is not a gate. Groundedness is computed from chunk ids rather than judgement — a citation whose chunk was not retrieved cannot have been read from a source.
nodes.norm_label: deterministic metrics gate ci; the llm judge is opt-in

nodes.label: Relevance Scored at Document Level
nodes.rationale: Chunk ids derive from chunk boundaries, so changing the chunker changes every id — chunk-level relevance would invalidate the golden set on precisely the experiment it exists to run.

nodes.label: fact_match Reported 1.0 for Work Never Done
nodes.rationale: Computed as "no expected fact was missing", so a --retrieval-only run that generated nothing had missed nothing — arithmetically correct, factually a lie. Fixed by omitting generation metrics entirely from a retrieval-only run: a metric that is absent is not a metric that is zero.
nodes.norm_label: fact_match reported 1.0 for work never done

nodes.label: Measured Quality Baseline
nodes.rationale: 86 golden cases over 21 documents / 193 chunks: recall@5 0.932, hit_rate@5 0.938, mrr 0.860, precision@5 0.190, citation_coverage 1.00, groundedness 1.00, citation_precision 0.732, fact_match 0.90, abstention_accuracy 0.80, latency_p50 12.6s, p95 92.9s. precision@5 of 0.190 is near its 0.2 ceiling because most cases have one relevant document in five slots — useful relatively, misleading absolutely.

nodes.label: docs/company Is the Corpus; docs/engineering Is Not
nodes.rationale: With the old `docs/` root an employee asking about refunds could be answered from an ADR about reciprocal rank fusion, with a correct citation, confidently — retrieval succeeds, grounding succeeds, the citation is right, the universe is wrong, and nothing downstream catches it. An exclusion list fails open; a directory boundary fails safe. The root is named in exactly two places (Makefile DOCS and cli/diagnose.py --corpus) and they must agree.
nodes.norm_label: docs/company is the corpus; docs/engineering is not

nodes.label: FAQ Split into 17 Topic Files
nodes.rationale: With a single-document corpus recall@k is 1.0 for every answerable question, so the retrieval metrics measure nothing. All 89 questions preserved verbatim; citations also improved from "Advance FAQ" to "Tax Display". The split fixed the measurement, not just the presentation.

nodes.label: Scoped LangChain Adoption
nodes.rationale: Adopt LangChain for undifferentiated work, keep OSC's own code where OSC's design is better. Adopted: text splitting, provider reach via a bridge, and outbound interoperability. Not adopted: the vector store (pgvector fuses lexical and vector search with RRF in SQL in one round trip; LangChain's PGVector does not), the retrieval pipeline (LCEL would obscure the path most in need of reading), the answer loop, prompts and tracing.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Provider Strategy
nodes.rationale: Native adapters are the default path and keep provider-specific capabilities (Anthropic's verified citations, reasoning controls on the OpenAI-compatible family); the LangChain bridge covers the long tail at the cost of marker-parsed citations and one more layer. The class is named by import path rather than resolved by init_chat_model, which would pull LangGraph in to save one configuration line.

nodes.label: Core Runtime Small, Vendor SDKs Are Extras
nodes.rationale: langchain-core and langchain-text-splitters are core dependencies because both are pure Python with no vendor SDK behind them and both must be importable for the registries to be complete. Every LangChain integration package stays an install-time choice named by the operator in options.class_path.
nodes.norm_label: core runtime small, vendor sdks are extras

nodes.label: One Datastore — PostgreSQL with pgvector
nodes.rationale: One database holds chunk text, embeddings, the generated tsvector lexical index and document metadata, so a chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip. The embedding dimension is substituted into the DDL at migration time and the HNSW index is created only when it is <= 2000.

nodes.label: workspace_id Partition Key From Day One
nodes.rationale: The only speculative design in the codebase, and defended on the grounds that adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration.
nodes.norm_label: workspace_id partition key from day one

nodes.label: Operator Errors Are Messages; Bugs Are Tracebacks
nodes.rationale: AssistantError is the vocabulary for problems an operator must fix and each carries an actionable message; a traceback buries it under frames describing our call stack rather than their problem. Anything else keeps its frames, because for a bug the frames are the point. Untranslated asyncpg errors surfaced as a bare OSError and bypassed the API's error handler entirely.
nodes.norm_label: operator errors are messages; bugs are tracebacks

nodes.label: Human Output on stderr, Machine Output on stdout
nodes.rationale: Two audiences served by two streams rather than by compromising one: `./osc serve > run.log` still yields a clean parseable log while the terminal shows where the service is listening and any startup note worth knowing.
nodes.norm_label: human output on stderr, machine output on stdout

nodes.label: Text Extraction Is a Plain Dict of Functions
nodes.rationale: A parser is selected by file extension and takes no options, so `PARSERS: dict[str, Parser]` is the whole mechanism — a registry would be an abstraction with nothing to configure. Parsers extract and never rewrite, because chunk text is quoted back as citation evidence and invented text would make that evidence a forgery.
nodes.norm_label: text extraction is a plain dict of functions

nodes.label: Unreadable Files Are Present, Not Deleted
nodes.rationale: FilesystemLoader records files it cannot read in `failures`, which the pipeline treats as present-but-unreadable rather than deleted — otherwise a corrupt file would destroy its own indexed copy.
nodes.norm_label: unreadable files are present, not deleted

nodes.label: 34 of 193 Chunks Are Exact Duplicates
nodes.rationale: Two scenario .docx files differ at the byte level but extract to byte-identical text (hash 54314756e14a2f4f), so they index twice and compete for the same top_k=5 slots. content_hash answers "has this document changed?" and never "is this the same as another document?". Smallest fix is a duplicates check in `./osc doctor` grouping by content hash.

nodes.label: Spreadsheet Chunks Are 42% of the Index
nodes.rationale: 82 of 193 chunks come from two .xlsx files and four of the six recall failures retrieved a spreadsheet chunk in place of the FAQ document that answers the question. Whether that is bad chunking of tabular data, bad ranking, or an under-specified golden set is undetermined — and is exactly the kind of question the harness makes answerable.
nodes.norm_label: spreadsheet chunks are 42% of the index

nodes.label: latency_p95 of 92.9s Against a 120s Provider Timeout
nodes.rationale: Measured under --concurrency 2 against a single Ollama instance, so partly contention and partly cold start; the observed p95 is within a factor of 1.3 of the point where requests fail rather than merely being slow, and nothing caps concurrency today.
nodes.norm_label: latency_p95 of 92.9s against a 120s provider timeout

nodes.label: The Local Model Misreads Figures
nodes.rationale: qwen3:8b rendered "500 to 2,500 EUR" as "50,000 to 2,500 EUR" while citing the correct passage — retrieval right, citation right, number wrong. The central honest caveat of the local stack, quantified as fact_match 0.90 but not yet reproduced under measurement.

nodes.label: Two Abstention Mechanisms, One Measured
nodes.rationale: The architectural guarantee (no hits, no model call) is solid; prose self-abstention is a model behaviour with no guarantee behind it. abstention_accuracy 0.80 scored a correct prose refusal as a miss because retrieval returned hits — the metric cannot yet distinguish the two mechanisms.

nodes.label: What the Knowledge Graph Says About the Structure
nodes.rationale: 2124 nodes, 4952 edges, 105 communities at 90% EXTRACTED. The logging subsystem forms the largest community (93 nodes), which is what a genuinely new subsystem should look like rather than code smeared across existing ones. Node count fell while edge count rose because document nodes moved from structural heading stubs to semantic concepts.
nodes.norm_label: what the knowledge graph says about the structure

nodes.label: Milestone A′ — Spend the Harness
nodes.rationale: The harness was built and not yet spent. A chunker comparison, a reranker decision, a top_k/rrf_k sweep and one hosted-provider run are each two commands and a recorded number; several have been waiting on a measurement for two phases, and leaving them unmeasured would be the worst outcome of this iteration.

nodes.label: Production Start-Up Guard
nodes.rationale: Endpoints are unauthenticated, unbounded and unthrottled; the service says so at startup when environment != development, but the constraint lives in prose rather than the code path. Refusing to start without configured auth outside development is ten lines and makes it enforced rather than announced.

nodes.label: A Retrieval Change Ships With a Measured Improvement
nodes.rationale: Chunk size, top_k, rrf_k, the chunking strategy, the reranker and query rewriting are all educated guesses; moving one without a before/after number is how the guesses became permanent. The default chunker stays `recursive` because switching it changes every chunk id in a live index and there was no golden set when the alternatives landed.
nodes.norm_label: a retrieval change ships with a measured improvement

nodes.label: The ./osc Operator CLI
nodes.rationale: Runs the CLI without activating the virtualenv or typing a path into it. Commands are grouped by purpose into three --help panels — running, understanding, looking at data — rather than listed flat, and every inspection command takes --json so they compose into scripts.

nodes.label: Diagnosis Workflow — doctor, traces, trace, search, chunk
nodes.rationale: Ordered so each step narrows the next: doctor names the broken component, `traces --failed` finds the request, `trace <id>` shows which stage raised, `search` separates "the model misread the passage" from "the passage was never retrieved", and `chunk <id>` shows the exact text the model was given.
nodes.norm_label: diagnosis workflow — doctor, traces, trace, search, chunk

nodes.label: Layered Configuration
nodes.rationale: Environment > .env > YAML profile, with any value addressable as OSC_ and __ for nesting. `./osc config` prints what actually resolved alongside the OSC_* variables that participated — the fast answer to "production is using the wrong model" — with credentials redacted unless --show-secrets.

nodes.label: Experiment Profiles
nodes.rationale: Copy a profile, change one thing, point OSC_PROFILE at it. hosted-anthropic is the only configuration with provider-verified citations; local-only swaps in sentence-transformers and the cross-encoder; groq-voyage shares no vendor with either; langchain-bridge reaches a provider through LangChain with heading-aware chunking. None requires a code change.

nodes.label: Idempotent Ingestion by Content Hash
nodes.rationale: Re-running over an unchanged corpus makes zero embedding calls; an edited file re-indexes alone and a deleted file is pruned with its chunks. One bad file cannot break a sync: it is reported, skipped, not pruned, and the command exits non-zero.

nodes.label: --reindex When the Chunker Changes
nodes.rationale: The content hash covers the document text and nothing else, so changing chunking.strategy, chunk_size or the embedding model leaves every stored chunk stale while every hash still matches — an ordinary sync would report `skipped` for the whole corpus and quietly keep the old chunks.

nodes.label: min_score Applies Before Reranking
nodes.rationale: First-stage scores are on a known scale; a cross-encoder logit is unbounded and often negative for a relevant passage, so thresholding reranker output would have emptied the result set the moment a reranker was enabled.

nodes.label: Tracing Is OSC's Own, Shaped Like OpenTelemetry
nodes.rationale: OTel is the right answer once traces leave the process, so trace.py is deliberately spans/parent-ids/attributes to make that day an exporter rather than a rewrite. LangChain callbacks were rejected for a stronger reason: they observe only LangChain runs, so a tracer built on them would be blind to chunking, pgvector's SQL fusion and the abstention decision.
nodes.norm_label: tracing is osc's own, shaped like opentelemetry

nodes.label: observability.capture_text
nodes.rationale: Keeps every timing, count and stage while recording only the length of any text, for a corpus where a trace must not contain content. The HTTP trace endpoints are additionally registered only in development, because traces carry question text and chunk ids and no endpoint is authenticated yet.

nodes.label: OSCRetriever — Outbound LangChain Interoperability
nodes.rationale: OSC's value is the indexed corpus and how it is retrieved, not the answer loop. Teams will build agents on frameworks OSC does not control, so making the pipeline consumable as a LangChain BaseRetriever means they use the same index and tuning rather than standing up a parallel one that drifts. integrations/ may import the core; the core may never import integrations/.

nodes.label: make test Asks If It Is Correct; make eval Asks If It Is Good
nodes.rationale: Different questions: a system can pass every test while answering every question badly, which is why evaluation is a separate command and not a test file. The suite runs the real pipelines against in-process protocol implementations registered through the ordinary registry, so "the whole stack can be retargeted by configuration alone" is asserted rather than assumed.
nodes.norm_label: make test asks if it is correct; make eval asks if it is good

nodes.label: The Empty-Index Startup Note
nodes.rationale: A service which starts perfectly and abstains from every question is indistinguishable from a broken model unless somebody thinks to look — so the banner says it before the first request.

nodes.label: The Logging System
nodes.rationale: What the system did, recorded durably — the other half of observability. Two streams under .osc/logs/, both fed through a queue with a trace-context filter and a redaction filter before any handler sees a record.

nodes.label: Logging and Tracing Answer Different Questions
nodes.rationale: A trace is a tree answering "how did this execution spend its time"; a log is a flat stream answering "what happened across all executions". A trace cannot tell you the same failure happened 40 times overnight; a log cannot show you which stage was slow. They are joined by exactly one field: trace_id.
nodes.norm_label: logging and tracing answer different questions

nodes.label: The Span Bridge
nodes.rationale: Logging does not add instrumentation; it subscribes to the instrumentation that exists. One hook in trace.py's span-exit path emits a TRACE record per stage, giving retrieve, embed_query, search, threshold, rerank, generate, finalise, load_hashes, document, chunk, embed, store and prune their log lines with no modification to any pipeline, provider, chunker or store. It costs one isEnabledFor check when unused.

nodes.label: trace_id Stamped on Every Log Record
nodes.rationale: A logging.Filter reads the tracer's context var and stamps it. Without this field, logs and traces are two piles of facts about the same request with nothing joining them; with it, any log line expands into a full waterfall via `./osc trace <id>`.
nodes.norm_label: trace_id stamped on every log record

nodes.label: Writing Is Off the Calling Thread
nodes.rationale: Every handler sits behind a QueueHandler/QueueListener pair so a log call costs an enqueue. Logging that blocks a request on fsync is logging that gets deleted the first time it appears in a latency profile. The cost is a background thread per process and records lost on a hard kill.
nodes.norm_label: writing is off the calling thread

nodes.label: Disk Bounded by Construction
nodes.rationale: max_bytes * (backup_count + 1), roughly 60 MB by default, with the oldest rotated file deleted rather than archived. The trade is that retention windows are not predictable — a quiet week keeps more history than a busy hour.

nodes.label: Redaction Filter and NEVER_REDACT
nodes.rationale: Matched on field name rather than value, because a value-inspecting heuristic both misses novel formats and mangles legitimate content. Applied on the queue entry rather than in a formatter, because a secret suppressed on disk and printed to stdout is a secret that leaked. The allowlist earned its place: input_tokens contains "token" and is a cost measurement.

nodes.label: Corpus Text Reduced to a Length
nodes.rationale: question, answer, query, text and prompt become `<47 chars>` unless capture_payloads is on — keeping every timing and count an investigation needs while keeping corpus content out of a file that tends to get shipped elsewhere. capture_payloads cannot re-enable credential redaction.
nodes.norm_label: corpus text reduced to a length

nodes.label: TRACE Level (5)
nodes.rationale: Somewhere to put per-stage detail that would be unbearable at DEBUG. Third-party libraries are pinned to WARNING regardless, because raising our level to watch our own pipeline must not turn on every vendor SDK's unstructured debug stream into a JSONL file.

nodes.label: The Console Can Be Quieter Than the File
nodes.rationale: An interactive CLI command prints its answer rather than a JSON stream, but the file keeps recording at the configured level. Quietening the terminal must not throw away the log, which is the easy mistake when one level controls both destinations — hence configure_logging's separate console_level.
nodes.norm_label: the console can be quieter than the file

nodes.label: The Audit Stream
nodes.rationale: One record per answered question, written from generation/answerer.py so both buffered and streaming paths are covered by one call site. Separate because operational logs roll off in hours under TRACE while "which passages did we show this user in March" must outlive that — one stream would mean one retention policy and the debug firehose would win. Pinned at INFO so raising the root level cannot silently stop recording.

nodes.label: The cli.command Record
nodes.rationale: Emitted by load(), which every command calls. Without it the log is a stream of identical settings.resolved and component.built records with no way to tell an ask from an ingest from a doctor, because every command initialises the same way. It reads sys.argv rather than the click context because typer invokes a callback outside the context click.get_current_context reads; the positional tail is payload and appears only under capture_payloads.

nodes.label: ./osc logs Is a Discovery Command, Not a Viewer
nodes.rationale: tail, grep and jq already read JSONL better than anything worth writing; the hard part is knowing which file to point them at once rotation has produced six.
nodes.norm_label: ./osc logs is a discovery command, not a viewer

nodes.label: ADR 0009 — Persistent Logging on the Standard Library, Fed by the Span Stream
nodes.rationale: Accepted, Phase 5. OSC had structured logging to stdout only across 30 call sites in 13 modules: no history, no correlation, no coverage, no level below DEBUG. The shaping constraint was that pipelines, providers, chunkers, the evaluation harness and the LangChain integration were out of scope for modification, so coverage had to come from somewhere other than new call sites in them.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009 — persistent logging on the standard library, fed by the span stream

nodes.label: Everything Else Is Stdlib
nodes.rationale: structlog and loguru are good and neither earns a dependency: the formatter is 15 lines, the filters 20, and rotation and async writing come from the standard library either way. A dependency would also put a third-party API on the one code path that must keep working while everything else is broken.

nodes.label: Size-Based Rotation, Not Time-Based
nodes.rationale: TimedRotatingFileHandler gives predictable windows and no ceiling at all — one busy day can produce an arbitrarily large file. For a service that can get busy, bounded disk is the guarantee worth having. Doing both needs a custom handler subclass for a guarantee size-based already provides.

nodes.label: Rejected — Hand-Written Log Lines in Every Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The obvious way to get coverage, and it would have meant editing retrieval, ingestion, generation, chunking and the providers — all out of scope — and maintaining a second set of instrumentation that drifts from the spans on the first change nobody makes twice.
nodes.norm_label: rejected — hand-written log lines in every pipeline

nodes.label: Rejected — Replace the Trace Store With Logs
nodes.rationale: Tempting — one persistence mechanism instead of two. Rejected because a trace is a tree and a log is a stream, and reassembling a waterfall from interleaved lines across concurrent requests is work the trace store already avoids. They persist separately and are joined by trace_id.
nodes.norm_label: rejected — replace the trace store with logs

nodes.label: QueueHandler.prepare() Strips exc_info
nodes.rationale: The stdlib strips exc_info to make records picklable across a process boundary. Our queue is consumed by a thread in the same process, so the stripping bought nothing and silently deleted every traceback — the worst thing a logging system can do quietly. Fixed with a prepare() override and a regression test.

nodes.label: The Failure Modes of a Logging System Are Silent
nodes.rationale: Both defects — stripped tracebacks and redacted token counts — were found by reading the output of a real run, not by construction and not by a test. The lesson recorded is that reading real output is the only way to find them.
nodes.norm_label: the failure modes of a logging system are silent

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: Builds a persistent knowledge graph from a repository — nodes for symbols, files and concepts, edges, community detection, and query/path/explain operations. Used so a new session navigates instead of recursively reading; it answers structural questions the code cannot (affected, god-nodes); and it acts as an outside observer on the architecture, usually right when it disagrees with the intended design.

nodes.label: A Test Double Was the Most Connected Node
nodes.rationale: An earlier build reported StubEmbeddingModel ahead of every real component — the graph's way of saying that the test suite, not production wiring, was what exercised every seam. It has since been displaced by MemoryVectorStore and Document. No architecture document would have surfaced that; it came from measuring the graph.
nodes.norm_label: a test double was the most connected node

nodes.label: Fewer Nodes, More Edges
nodes.rationale: 2086/4572 became 1981/4624 — density 2.19 to 2.33 — because 429 structural heading stubs were replaced by 324 semantic concepts carrying rationale, citations and hyperedges. When a rebuild shrinks, check the edge count before assuming loss; to_json's shrink guard exists to force exactly that check.

nodes.label: Rebuilding Needs the office and sql Extras
nodes.rationale: Without `office` the four scenario documents are reported as skipped_sensitive and silently dropped, which hid ~42% of the real corpus from the graph for two phases; without `sql`, migrations/001_init.sql contributes nothing. `graphify update` is AST-only and will not pick up changed prose in docs/, so editing documentation needs a full rebuild plus `graphify export wiki` or wiki/ silently describes the previous graph.
nodes.norm_label: rebuilding needs the office and sql extras

nodes.label: Dangling-Endpoint Edges Are Mostly Not a Defect
nodes.rationale: Of 273 in a full rebuild, 245 were imports edges pointing at third-party packages and stdlib — the graph declining to invent nodes for things outside the corpus, not losing them. Only ~17 were genuine unresolved cross-chunk references. The incremental build reports 0 because build_merge resolves against the graph it merges into rather than one chunk.
nodes.norm_label: dangling-endpoint edges are mostly not a defect

nodes.label: Ponytail
nodes.rationale: A development discipline forcing the laziest solution that actually works, on the claim that the best code is the code never written. It makes the handbook's "avoid unnecessary abstractions" operational — a checklist that runs before code is written rather than a principle invoked during review, when the code exists and deleting it feels like waste. The targeted failure mode is specific: a RAG platform invites a plugin system for retrievers, a rules engine for chunking, an abstraction over the abstraction.

nodes.label: The Ponytail Ladder
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: does this need to exist at all, is it already in this codebase, does the standard library do it, does a native platform feature cover it, does an installed dependency solve it, can it be one line, and only then the minimum code that works.

nodes.label: Lazy at the Core, Strict at the Edges
nodes.rationale: Input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security measures and anything explicitly requested are never simplified away — which is why settings.py, api/schemas.py and evaluation/dataset.py use full Pydantic validation while types.py uses bare frozen dataclasses. The domain types are constructed internally; the other three parse untrusted input.
nodes.norm_label: lazy at the core, strict at the edges

nodes.label: The ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: A deliberate simplification that cuts a real corner with a known ceiling is marked in the source, naming the ceiling and the upgrade path. This is what makes the discipline safe rather than merely fast: a shortcut with a named upgrade path is a decision, an unmarked one is technical debt nobody remembers taking on. Currently one marker exists, in observability/store.py.

nodes.label: Testing Architecture (Four Tiers)
nodes.rationale: Four tiers, each answering a different question. The organising goal is confidence, not coverage — a suite is judged by what it lets you believe, not by percentage of lines executed.

nodes.label: Unit / Component Tier (make test)
nodes.rationale: 320 tests answering 'is the logic correct?' with no network, database or credential, in ~2s, so they run anywhere and always. Speed and zero external dependency are what make the tier something a developer actually runs, rather than something CI runs after the mistake has shipped.

nodes.label: Integration Tier (make test-integration)
nodes.rationale: 18 pgvector tests answering 'does the SQL do what we think?'. SQL semantics cannot be asserted against a stub — only a real PostgreSQL can tell you whether the query means what it reads as.

nodes.label: End-to-End Tier (make test-e2e)
nodes.rationale: 9 tests against live Ollama AND PostgreSQL, answering whether the whole thing works against real infrastructure. Requires a machine with both, which is why it is a separate tier rather than part of the default run.

nodes.label: Evaluation Tier (make eval)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly not a test but a measurement, run after `make ingest`. Kept as a distinct tier because correctness and quality are different properties and conflating them hides the second one.

nodes.label: Correctness vs Goodness Distinction
nodes.rationale: `make test` asks whether the system is correct; `make eval` asks whether it is good. Named as the distinction worth internalising because a system can pass every test and still answer every question badly — a green suite is not evidence of a useful assistant.

nodes.label: Protocol-Layer In-Process Doubles
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful
nodes.rationale: conftest.py holds in-process implementations of the protocols — not mocks. Because a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, the fast tier exercises the real pipelines rather than a special test-only code path. This is the direct payoff from choosing protocols over abstract base classes.

nodes.label: conftest.py (Shared Fixtures and Isolation)
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful, § Rules
nodes.rationale: Single place holding the protocol doubles and the per-test isolation: redirects trace and log directories to tmp_path and calls shutdown_logging() on teardown, since the log listener is a background thread and a leaked one writes a later test's records into a deleted tmp_path.

nodes.label: StubEmbeddingModel
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful
nodes.rationale: Deterministic bag-of-words embedder hashing tokens into buckets, so texts sharing vocabulary land near each other under cosine similarity. Chosen over a random or constant stub because it makes retrieval assertions meaningful and identical on every machine with no model download.

nodes.label: StubChatModel
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful
nodes.rationale: Returns a scripted reply but goes through the real marker-parsing citation path, so citation handling is genuinely exercised rather than bypassed.

nodes.label: Registering Doubles Through the Ordinary Registry
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful
nodes.rationale: API and CLI tests register the doubles through the same registry path a new provider takes, so the claim 'the whole stack can be retargeted by configuration alone' is asserted by the suite rather than assumed by the architecture document.
nodes.norm_label: registering doubles through the ordinary registry

nodes.label: provider-architecture.md (Protocols Not ABCs)
nodes.source_location: § What makes the fast tier meaningful, § Related
nodes.rationale: Cited as the reason the doubles are legitimate: protocols rather than base classes is what allows a test double to be indistinguishable from a provider.

nodes.label: evaluation.md (The Fourth Tier)
nodes.rationale: Referenced for the fourth tier and why it is not a test.

nodes.label: Regression Test For Every Found Defect
nodes.rationale: A found defect gets a regression test in the same commit. The bold coverage rows are that policy's output and are called the highest-value category of test in the suite — which is why the coverage list is kept visible rather than deleted as noise.
nodes.norm_label: regression test for every found defect

nodes.label: Rule: Tests Never Touch the Production Corpus
nodes.rationale: docs/company/ is real company knowledge; a test asserting against it would start failing the day someone edited an FAQ answer — a false alarm and the fastest way to get a suite disabled. Every test builds its own fixtures instead.
nodes.norm_label: rule: tests never touch the production corpus

nodes.label: The test_e2e.py Corpus-Root Violation and Repair
nodes.rationale: test_e2e.py ingested Path("docs") directly — harmless while that directory held demonstration data, and two defects the moment it held real content: the suite asserted against editable company documents AND swept docs/engineering/ into its index, retrieving the knowledge base. Repaired by having test_ingestion.py assert the Makefile and CLI corpus roots agree and that the knowledge base is not reachable from the corpus root.
nodes.norm_label: the test_e2e.py corpus-root violation and repair

nodes.label: Rule: Tests Never Write Into the Working Directory
nodes.rationale: Trace and log persistence both default to on and write under .osc/. Redirecting both to tmp_path also stops one test's records being visible to the next, which would make CLI assertions order-dependent.
nodes.norm_label: rule: tests never write into the working directory

nodes.label: Environment-Purge Isolation Defect (OSC_LOGGING__DIRECTORY)
nodes.rationale: test_cli.py deletes every OSC_* variable to prove commands can be retargeted through configuration alone — which also deletes the isolation conftest installed. It re-applied OSC_OBSERVABILITY__TRACE_DIR but not OSC_LOGGING__DIRECTORY, so every CLI test wrote into the developer's real .osc/logs. Caught by watching the file grow during a run; the two overrides now sit adjacent with a comment naming both.

nodes.label: Rule: A Test Asserts a Behaviour, Not an Implementation
nodes.rationale: test_store_contract is parametrised over store implementations; a new store is added to the parametrisation and is then held to exactly the same behaviour as the existing ones — the contract, not the internals, is what is pinned.
nodes.norm_label: rule: a test asserts a behaviour, not an implementation

nodes.label: test_store_contract (Parametrised Store Contract)
nodes.rationale: The concrete mechanism for behaviour-not-implementation testing: one parametrised contract every store implementation must satisfy.

nodes.label: test_logging.py
nodes.rationale: Covers log creation, rotation, retention and the disk ceiling; console/file level separation; trace-id correlation; the span bridge on/off; redaction of credentials and payloads; the invoked command and flags with the positional tail gated on capture_payloads; audit-stream isolation and independent retention; unwritable directories; tracebacks surviving the queue; token counts not read as credentials.

nodes.label: test_evaluation.py
nodes.rationale: Metrics against worked examples; golden-set validation; failed cases excluded from means; retrieval-only omits generation metrics; judge verdict parsing and failure handling.

nodes.label: test_cli.py
nodes.rationale: Every operational command; doctor's pass/warn/fail; trace commands across process boundaries; operator-error reporting; help grouping. Also the suite that purges OSC_* to prove configuration-only retargeting.

nodes.label: test_langchain_integration.py
nodes.rationale: Both chunkers (id stability, content preservation, size budget, heading metadata); chat and embedding bridges; the outbound retriever.

nodes.label: test_pgvector_integration.py
nodes.rationale: Migrations, tsvector, SQL fusion, cascade delete, JSONB, workspace isolation, transaction rollback, inspection SQL. Shares the application database — isolation is by workspace_id only, a known gap.

nodes.label: test_fusion_and_grounding.py
nodes.rationale: RRF ordering and dedup; citation marker parsing; prompt-injection containment (a regression for a real defect).

nodes.label: test_api.py
nodes.rationale: Health, status, search, chat (both modes), SSE ordering, trace endpoints and their environment gate; per-request correlation ids and the request/response log pair.

nodes.label: test_trace_store.py
nodes.rationale: Cross-process readability, rotation, malformed lines, unwritable directories, round-trip fidelity.

nodes.label: test_observability.py
nodes.rationale: Span tree shape, nested-trace merging, error capture, span cap, text redaction.

nodes.label: test_retrieval.py
nodes.rationale: Store contract, all three strategies, top_k, reranking, rewriting, and min_score applied pre-rerank (a regression for a real defect).

nodes.label: test_parsers.py
nodes.rationale: Every format, content preservation, corrupt and scanned files, empty workbooks, and failure isolation (a regression for a real defect).

nodes.label: test_ingestion.py
nodes.rationale: Idempotency, change detection, pruning, unreadable-file prune exemption, --reindex, trace shape. Also the guard that the Makefile and CLI corpus roots agree and the knowledge base is unreachable from the corpus root.

nodes.label: test_chunking.py
nodes.rationale: Size budget, id stability, and content preservation (a regression for a real defect).

nodes.label: test_server_lifecycle.py
nodes.rationale: Startup notes, in-flight stream failure emits a terminal event (a regression for a real defect), shutdown releases only what was built.

nodes.label: test_inspection.py
nodes.rationale: StoreInspector contract; empty-store edge cases.

nodes.label: test_answerer.py
nodes.rationale: Abstention in both modes, citation policy, streaming reassembly.

nodes.label: test_settings.py
nodes.rationale: Four-layer precedence, nested env merge, malformed profiles, trace exposure gate.

nodes.label: test_e2e.py
nodes.rationale: Six formats indexed from a corpus it generates itself in tmp_path; idempotency; hybrid ranking; a cited answer; abstention; PDF text extraction proven via a hand-assembled minimal PDF so no rendering dependency is needed; both modes agreeing; the run fully traced. Takes a separate database, which is called the right pattern.

nodes.label: test_reasoning_models.py
nodes.rationale: <think> stripping, exhausted-budget error, reasoning markers never becoming citations.

nodes.label: test_registry.py
nodes.rationale: Registration, override, unknown-provider error.

nodes.label: Gap: No Hosted Provider Has Ever Been Called
nodes.rationale: Every hosted adapter is exercised only via stubs — including the Anthropic native-citation path, the only verified-citation implementation in the codebase. Its correctness is asserted by reading the SDK docs, not by a test. This is the direct cost of the stub-based fast tier and is stated rather than hidden.
nodes.norm_label: gap: no hosted provider has ever been called

nodes.label: Gap: No Load or Concurrency Test
nodes.rationale: Behaviour under parallel requests and the connection-pool bounds are untested. `./osc eval --concurrency N` is the closest thing to one and was not built for that purpose.
nodes.norm_label: gap: no load or concurrency test

nodes.label: Gap: Gemini Adapters Hold an Unreleasable HTTP Client
nodes.rationale: Six of eight adapters implement aclose(); genai.Client exposes no async close in the installed surface and is an optional extra, so the gap is recorded rather than guessed at.
nodes.norm_label: gap: gemini adapters hold an unreleasable http client

nodes.label: Gap: pgvector Suite Shares the Application Database
nodes.rationale: Isolation is by workspace_id and it is honoured, but a run against a production DSN would write to production. The e2e suite's separate database is the right pattern the pgvector suite should follow.
nodes.norm_label: gap: pgvector suite shares the application database

nodes.label: Gap: No CI
nodes.rationale: make check, make eval-gate and the suites all exist; nothing runs them automatically on a pull request, so every guarantee above depends on a human remembering.

nodes.label: Principle: State the Gaps Plainly
nodes.rationale: A testing document that claims completeness is not useful. Enumerating what is untested is what lets a reader calibrate how much the green suite is worth.
